messages:
alex: Heads up — after today's v2 soft-rollout we saw ~3x increase in v1 quota hits for a single customer. Console QPS shows shift but routing logs indicate requests routed to v2. Anyone else seeing a mismatch? :thinking:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered for v2 at 09:13 UTC by @alex

maria: I noticed dashboard metric `quota_consume.v1` spiked for a few accounts, but the routing logs we pull (route=v2) don't line up. Could be telemetry tagging vs billing tagging divergence.

esha: I pulled raw logs for acme-corp. Request ids: 7f1a3b6e, 7f1a3b7a, 7f1a3b99 — headers show `x-api-version: 2` and route=v2, but billing tag `billing_api_version=v1`. Looks like the billing pipeline is applying a token->version mapping.

sam: Quick repro using curl:```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer old-token-xyz" -H "x-api-version: 2" https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```Response routed to v2, but internal billing tag for that request was v1 in the event.

jen: We added a compatibility shim last quarter that maps legacy tokens to v1 for billing back-compat. I thought it only affected legacy endpoints, but it might still be tagging events. cc @esha — could be leaking at the billing-transform layer.

alex: If billing pipeline is using token mapping as source of truth, that's wrong. Routing should be authoritative. We need a clear split: route_version (what runtime served) vs billed_version (what billing pipeline tags). Right now they're inconsistent.

maria: Proposal: emit both `route_version` and `billed_version` as metrics per request, plus a boolean `version_discrepancy`. Add a small console panel showing discrepancy rate by account and a heatmap over time.

esha: For a quick mitigation: flip the shim into "tombstone" mode where it still accepts legacy tokens but does NOT mutate billing tags. Safe to do? How many customers rely on billed_version=v1?

sam: Ran quick counts over the last 24h: acme-corp: 432 discrepant events, beta-startup: 12, internal-test: 780 (most are internal dev tokens). So customer-facing impact is primarily acme-corp.

jen: I can push a tiny shim patch to canary that stops tagging billing events with legacy mapping. Patch is 2 lines + a feature flag. Want me to deploy to 10% canary?

alex: Yes deploy to 10% canary. Add an alert: discrepancy_rate > 0.5% for any account should page/ping oncall. Also create a ticket to remove shim entirely in next milestone.

maria: Created INF-2392 with checklist: 1) emit route_version & billed_version metrics, 2) add discrepancy panel, 3) canary shim flip, 4) customer comms. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/inf-versions (internal).

deploy-bot: Canary patch deployed to 10% of traffic at 11:05 UTC by jen

esha: Monitoring update: for canary traffic discrepancy rate dropped from 2.8% -> 0.02% within 30m. Will watch for 2h before rolling.

sam: Also note we should update API contract/docs: token->version mapping is deprecated and will be removed. Add a changelog entry and a migration note for token owners.

jen: I'll open the changelog PR and email affected customers with a 30-day grace notice. :thumbsup:

alex: Good. Follow-up: add a short-lived telemetry bucket with raw headers + token mapping for discrepant requests for 7 days for debug. Esha, can you take INF-2393 to wire that?

esha: On it. Filing INF-2393 and will attach sample of 10 request ids and the raw event payloads.

alex: Closing loop — keep the console panel up, alerting in place, and plan to remove shim next sprint unless customers push back. Great catch team :rocket:
